headline: High risk of shared-workspace write conflicts and medium prompt-injection/cascade risks; no direct evidence of a shared channel or compliance mismatch.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A writes skill files and builds on shared context, while agent B can read/write files and run browsers. That creates a plausible path where A’s content is consumed by B as trusted input, even though no explicit shared channel is documented. Uncertainty about the bridge escalates this above low.
conditions: IF agent A’s generated files are fed into agent B’s pipeline without sanitization, injection is possible.
IF agent B parses A-authored markdown or scripts as instructions, attacker-controlled content can steer behavior.
mitigations: Add a strict content boundary between A outputs and B inputs.
Require allowlisted schemas for any A-to-B handoff.
Strip executable directives from shared files before B reads them.
Review one sample A output before enabling automated ingestion.
requires-engineering: add provenance tags to all inter-agent artifacts.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents can read and write the filesystem, and A touches marketing/product-marketing context while B processes broad multimodal content. A shared workspace could expose A’s files to B and vice versa. No direct evidence shows sensitive classes like PHI or secrets, so medium fits the default shared-workspace risk.
conditions: IF both agents mount the same workspace directory, file contents can cross between them.
IF B ingests files from A’s workspace, A’s marketing context may be exposed in B outputs.
mitigations: Separate workspaces per agent.
Remove shared mounts from the runtime config.
Audit one directory listing for overlap before launch.
Disable automatic file ingestion in B for A-owned paths.
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent filesystem sandboxing.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Both agents have unrestricted filesystem write, subprocess spawning, and multiple-instance support. In a shared directory, concurrent edits can clobber files or corrupt generated artifacts. Because neither profile mentions locking or coordination, the conflict pathway is plausible in default multi-instance use and can cause irreversible workspace loss.
conditions: IF both agents write to the same directory concurrently, file clobbering can occur.
IF either agent modifies shared build or model files without locks, state corruption is possible.
mitigations: Run the agents in separate directories.
Serialize write operations manually for one session.
Use read-only mounts for one agent during testing.
Check for overlapping output paths before execution.
requires-engineering: add file locks or transactional writes.

D_cascading_error.rationale: A produces marketing content and shared context, and B has a pipeline API plus browser and shell execution. If B treats A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream generated artifacts or actions. The pair lacks any documented verification step, but B is not explicitly an autonomous action agent, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF B consumes A’s output without validation, A’s mistakes can propagate.
IF B uses A-generated text as prompts or configuration, downstream outputs may be wrong.
mitigations: Insert a human review step between A and B.
Require B to cite or validate A-derived claims.
Limit A-to-B transfer to structured fields only.
Run one end-to-end test with a known bad input.
requires-engineering: add automated verification gates.

E_compliance.rationale: No residency, certification, retention, or subject-rights mismatch is documented for either agent. A is open-source marketing tooling and B is open-source transformers; the profiles do not show regulated data handling. Because the rubric requires a documented gap for higher severity, the compliance risk remains low and mostly hypothetical.
conditions: IF regulated data is introduced into either agent, compliance review becomes necessary.
IF deployment policies require specific retention or residency controls, the current profiles do not document them.
mitigations: Avoid sending regulated data to the pair.
Check deployment region settings before use.
Review retention defaults in the runtime.
Document any compliance assumptions in the runbook.
requires-engineering: add policy enforcement for regulated datasets.
